events.title: Slavery Abolition Act Takes Effect in the British Empire
events.description: The Slavery Abolition Act 1833 came into force, abolishing slavery across most of the British Empire. Roughly 800,000 enslaved people in the Caribbean, Cape Colony and Canada were legally freed, though many were required to serve as apprentices for several more years.
events.significance: It marked a major milestone in the global anti-slavery movement and set a precedent for abolition in other nations, though enslavers rather than the formerly enslaved received financial compensation.

events.title: Joseph Priestley Isolates Oxygen
events.description: English chemist Joseph Priestley heated mercuric oxide with a lens and produced a gas that made flames burn brighter, which he called 'dephlogisticated air.' This gas was later named oxygen by Antoine Lavoisier.
events.significance: The discovery of oxygen transformed chemistry, overturned the phlogiston theory, and laid the groundwork for modern understanding of combustion and respiration.

events.title: Germany Declares War on Russia
events.description: Germany declared war on Russia, setting in motion the full mobilization of the great powers of Europe. The declaration followed Russia's mobilization in support of Serbia after Austria-Hungary's declaration of war on Serbia.
events.significance: This was a decisive step in the outbreak of World War I, a conflict that killed millions and reshaped the political map of Europe and the world.

events.title: Warsaw Uprising Begins
events.description: The Polish Home Army launched an uprising against Nazi German occupation in Warsaw as Soviet forces approached the city. The fighting lasted 63 days and ended in defeat for the insurgents, with the city largely destroyed afterward.
events.significance: It was the largest single military effort by any European resistance movement in World War II and remains a powerful symbol of Polish resistance, with an estimated 150,000 to 200,000 civilians killed.

events.title: MTV Launches
events.description: Music Television (MTV) premiered in the United States at 12:01 a.m., opening with the song 'Video Killed the Radio Star' by The Buggles.
events.significance: MTV revolutionized the music industry and popular culture by making music videos a central promotional and artistic form, shaping youth culture for decades.
